problem: Existing VLN maps (topological, BEV, grid memories) are hand-designed and built independently of the navigation policy, then consumed as fixed inputs. This causes a mismatch between what the map encodes and what the policy needs.
motivation: Partial observability makes spatial aggregation essential in VLN, but maps need not be exhaustive reconstructions. If a map is learned inside the decision loop, it can keep only navigation-critical information and be shaped by task rewards.
key_idea: Cast map construction as autoregressive BEV image synthesis (Janus-Pro) that outputs a compact 3-channel map for a VLM policy, then jointly optimize map generator and policy with GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning.
insight: Compact maps suffice: shrinking the BEV from 384x384/576 tokens to 96x96/36 tokens costs only about 1 SR (43.1 vs 42.2) while latency drops from 12.7s to 1.3s. RFT gives consistent gains over SPT (SR 42.2 to 45.6, SPL 36.5 to 40.5) and largely erases differences between channel initializations (final SR 43.6-45.6). Adding maps to a no-map baseline lifts SR from 37.7 to 42.2 after SPT. Note the ablations use a weaker config than the main result.
method: Map-in-the-loop architecture: the map module G takes the observation history, current frame and instruction and autoregressively generates a BEV map M_t; the policy consumes M_t plus the observations and instruction and predicts N=3 future actions.

Task-driven map supervision: a 3-channel BEV image made of Occupancy (values 0/128/255 for impassable/unobserved/traversable), Distance (relative geodesic-to-goal, truncated to [0,255]) and Landmark (instruction-referenced static objects from IRef-VLA labels).
Stage 1 map pre-training: Janus-Pro is trained with a token-level autoregressive loss on ground-truth BEV maps (extended to multi-image and text input), then frozen for stage-1 policy training.
Stage 1 policy pre-training: NVILA-2B is trained with cross-entropy over the next 3 actions on oracle plus DAgger data, conditioned on the generated maps.
Stage 2 joint RFT: GRPO with rollout size 8 and clip 0.28, jointly updating map module and policy. The importance ratio is the product of the policy ratio and the map-generation ratio.
Rewards: action reward for the longest correct prefix of the 3-step action sequence, plus a format-validity reward.

setting.backbone: Janus-Pro (map generator) + NVILA-2B (VLN policy), fine-tuned with SFT then GRPO
setting.model_size: NVILA-2B policy plus Janus-Pro (size not stated; likely 1B/7B)
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE trajectories converted to 1200K step-level state-action pairs, plus 500K non-oracle exploratory rollout samples and DAgger data; BEV labels from Habitat and IRef-VLA landmark annotations
setting.observation: monocular RGB with history frames and instruction; generated BEV map
setting.action_space: low-level discrete continuous-env actions, predicted as a sequence of 3 future actions
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE / RxR-CE); real world Unitree G1 humanoid
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT BEV maps only used as training supervision)

results: MapDream reaches 59.8 SR / 54.4 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 59.4 SR / 49.2 SPL on RxR-CE val-unseen with monocular RGB. This beats monocular baselines such as MonoDream (55.8/49.1), NaVILA (54.0/49.0) and Dynam3D, and its SPL even exceeds the panoramic BEVBert-based methods. Trained on R2R-CE only, it gets 27.8 SR on RxR-CE, beating sim2real (25.5) and MonoDream (25.1).
limitations: Only a local egocentric BEV is kept; there is no persistent global map over long horizons.
Temporal consistency of generated maps across timesteps is not enforced.
Map-generation latency is high at high resolution (12.7s per step), and map supervision needs GT simulator data and landmark annotations.
